title.narrative: The Gendered Impacts of Employment on Domestic Violence and Pyschosocial Wellbeing

description.narrative: This study seeks to generate evidence on the relationship between the experience of employment – as distinct from cash transfers alone – and intimate partner violence, intra-household bargaining power, and gendered perceptions of self-worth vis-à-vis one’s family and the community at large. We do so in the context of the Rohingya refugee camps, the largest refugee camps in the world, and a setting in which pervasive unemployment, strong gender norms, and high rates of domestic violence mark daily refugee experience. We hope the findings of this work may inform the design of social protection policies for the world’s forcibly displaced and long-term unemployed in the developing world. The Harvard Center for International Development offers sponsored research administration services to its HKS affiliated faculty which focus on promoting and amplifying faculty research.
